subject: FintechCo — Multi-region performance & competitive follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: FintechCo — post-demo: multi-region perf, next steps

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Primary ask: validate multi-region latency and data residency options for your fraud scoring pipeline (EU/US).
- Acceptance criteria you mentioned: p95 latency target for edge scoring <= 120ms, support for private VPC deployment for EU data.
- Immediate blockers: procurement questions (SOC 2 / DPA) and a short competitive checklist vs your current hyperscaler endpoints.

Our proposed next steps (we can start as soon as you give the go-ahead):
1) Share short competitive comparison doc and baseline latency runs (attached).
2) Run a multi-region perf test from your sample traffic (us-east, eu-west). We’ll provide scripts and analyze p50/p95, cold vs warm, and tail behavior.
3) Validate data residency options: hosted in EU, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private on-prem/VPC for strict residency.

Can you confirm you’re OK with us running a short read-only test against a staging endpoint? If yes, can you share a test endpoint or a small sample of representative requests (no PII)?

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (summary + cost model)

Proposed times to kick off: Mon 11/16 or Tue 11/17 — what works for you?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192]

[Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (PDF)]

Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo: multi-region perf, next steps

Thanks Jordan — good notes. A few quick clarifying items before we schedule tests: 

- Data residency: EU residency is required for customer PII processing. We can start with read-only traffic that is synthetic (no PII). If results look good, procurement will push for Private/Dedicated.
- Latency acceptance: our internal bar is p95 < 120ms for single-token/short prompt scoring (consistent with what I mentioned). How does Redwood measure p95 (server-side vs client-side)?
- Cost: curious about the cost delta vs our current hyperscaler endpoints — your doc should cover that but a quick summary would help.
- Compliance: please attach SOC 2 attestation or a link to your compliance page.

If the tests are read-only and synthetic, we can share a staging endpoint and a small sample (JSON). I can coordinate with our SRE to open a temp allowlist for your test IPs.

Asha
Head of ML Platform
FintechCo

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo: multi-region perf, next steps

Thanks — great questions. Short answers first, details below and attached: 

- Data residency: Redwood supports regionally-hosted endpoints in both EU (eu-west) and US (us-east). For strict residency we can offer Dedicated capacity or Private VPC deployments; both are compatible with your requirements.
- p95 measurement: we report server-side latency (inference time + network hop to our edge). For client-side numbers we can instrument a short script you run from your environment and we’ll correlate.
- SOC 2: attaching the attestation link in the doc and our compliance page.
- Cost delta: high-level — hyperscalers typically charge X for single-instance endpoints; with our batching/caching and optimized kernels customers often see 20-40% lower per-token unit cost for inference workloads like yours. Exact numbers depend on model, quantization, and batching profile; see attached cost model.

Attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (includes cost model) and latency_test_results_20261112.csv (baseline internal test). Also shared a test plan link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDeF_shared_test_plan

Proposed test matrix (we recommend starting small then scale):
- Phase A (sanity): 500 synthetic requests from us-east and eu-west, measure p50/p95, cold vs warm.
- Phase B (scale): 1k concurrent simulated requests with your typical payload size, capture tail latency and error rates.
- Phase C (production-like): replicate with larger contexts and validate KV cache / prefix behavior.

We can run Phase A as early as Mon 11/16. For allowlist: can you send a single staging URL and the IPs/hostnames you want us to use? We’ll run the tests over a one-hour window and share raw logs + summarized P50/P95.

Attachments: 
- [Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (PDF)]
- [Attachment: latency_test_results_20261112.csv (CSV)]
- Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FT-4821

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FintechCo — Multi-region performance & competitive follow-up

Hi Asha — looping in a short test-plan and what we’ll need from your side to run Phase A on Mon 11/16: 

Planned Phase A (sanity) test plan (summary):
- Duration: 60 minutes
- Traffic: 500 synthetic requests per region (us-east, eu-west) — payloads attached as sample_requests.json in the shared doc.
- Metrics: p50, p95, p99, error rate, cold vs warm (first token vs subsequent tokens), and throughput.
- Environment: staging endpoint you provide (read-only, synthetic traffic).
- Deliverables: aggregated CSV + visual dashboard, and recommendations for cluster config (batching/quantization) to meet p95 target.

What we need from FintechCo:
1) Staging endpoint (URL) + guardrail allowlist window (IP(s) and schedule).
2) Representative request samples (JSON) or confirmation to use our synthetic samples.
3) A point-of-contact from SRE to confirm allowlist and troubleshoot network.

If you’re comfortable, please share the staging URL and an allowlist window (we recommend 11/16 09:00–11:00 PT). We’ll also drop in a short monitoring Slack channel for live updates.

Forwarding a quick internal note from Sean on capacity sizing:

> From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
> To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

> Subject: internal — suggested sizing for Phase B
> 
> For Phase B (1k concurrent) we should reserve a small Dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Suggest 2x small GPU nodes for isolated runs; can revert to hosted for shorter sanity runs.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the test run and share results within 24h of completion.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
